title: Breaking the paradigm: record quindecim-charged magnetic ionic liquids

material_class.structural_family: pentanuclear rare-earth carboxylate ionic-liquid cluster cation

synthesis.procedure: A mixture of 10 mmol of the respective lanthanide sesquioxide and 1-carboxymethyl-3-ethylimidazolium chloride (11.438 g, 60 mmol) was stirred in 100 mL of water under reflux for 24 h. Solid Li[Tf2N] (17.22 g, 60 mmol) was added to the hot solution and stirring continued for 30 min. After cooling to room temperature a hydrophobic phase separated; the aqueous supernatant was decanted, residual phase separation was allowed over a few days, and the ionic liquid was decanted, washed with 40 mL water at room temperature, and separated in a separatory funnel as a pink hydrophobic liquid. The product was heated at 100 °C for 5 h and left in a Petri dish (150 × 15 mm) under ambient conditions. Single crystals of 1 suitable for X-ray diffraction were collected after 3–4 months.
synthesis.temperature: reflux, then room temperature; product heated at 100 °C
synthesis.time: 24 h reflux, then 30 min after Li[Tf2N] addition; crystallization over 3–4 months
synthesis.vessel_or_method: aqueous reflux, phase separation, separatory funnel, Petri-dish crystallization under ambient conditions
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Decantation of the aqueous phase, water wash, separatory-funnel isolation, heating at 100 °C for 5 h, then ambient crystallization; crystals of 1 after 3–4 months.

properties.summary: Room-temperature χT is close to five non-interacting Er(III) ions and falls on cooling; the liquid-state effective moment is 21.2 μB and magnetization at 2 K does not saturate. Compound 1 shows Er(III) NIR emission in both liquid and solid states with a lifetime of 0.6 ms.

material_class.structural_family: pentanuclear rare-earth carboxylate ionic-liquid cluster cation, isotypic with the Er analogue

synthesis.procedure: Prepared by the shared aqueous procedure: 10 mmol of the respective lanthanide sesquioxide and 1-carboxymethyl-3-ethylimidazolium chloride (11.438 g, 60 mmol) were refluxed in 100 mL water for 24 h, then Li[Tf2N] (17.22 g, 60 mmol) was added to the hot solution and stirring continued for 30 min. After cooling, the hydrophobic ionic-liquid phase was decanted, washed with 40 mL water, isolated with a separatory funnel, heated at 100 °C for 5 h, and left in a Petri dish under ambient conditions. Crystals of the Ho ionic liquid form after months under ambient conditions; the Er and Ho compounds are isotypic.

properties.summary: Room-temperature χT agrees with five non-interacting Ho(III) ions and decreases sharply below about 150 K. The liquid-state effective moment is 23.2–23.3 μB class, the highest of the series (23.3 μB), and low-temperature magnetization does not saturate. Compound 2 shows Ho(III) NIR emission with a lifetime of 0.8 ms.

synthesis.procedure: Prepared by the shared aqueous procedure used for 1–3: 10 mmol of the respective lanthanide sesquioxide and 1-carboxymethyl-3-ethylimidazolium chloride (11.438 g, 60 mmol) were refluxed in 100 mL water for 24 h, Li[Tf2N] (17.22 g, 60 mmol) was added, and the mixture was stirred for 30 min. The hydrophobic phase was isolated by decantation and separatory funnel after a water wash (40 mL), heated at 100 °C for 5 h, and left in a Petri dish. All crystallization attempts for the Tm ionic liquid failed; only glass transitions were observed.
